summary.allegation: The cardholder says Roastline Coffee Co charged their card twice for £54.00 on 12 April 2025 and that only one purchase was actually made, so one of the two charges is a duplicate.
summary.to_defend: The merchant must show the two £54.00 charges were two distinct purchases, each with its own purchase documentation, timestamp and authorisation code.

requirements.title: Two separate purchases
requirements.text: Evidence the two transactions are for two separate purchases (e.g. different order IDs, different items, different services rendered).
requirements.finding: The two charges carry different order IDs (RL-ORDER-44188 and RL-ORDER-44192), different invoice numbers (RL-88291 and RL-88294) and entirely different baskets — coffee beans in one, an Aeropress Go kit and filter papers in the other — placed roughly eleven hours apart on the same day. The identical £54.00 totals arise from a £6.00 loyalty discount applied to the first order's £60.00 basket.

requirements.title: Each purchase documented
requirements.text: Documentation of each purchase event (separate invoices, separate delivery confirmations, separate service dates).
requirements.finding: Two separate invoices document each purchase event, each showing its own order date, itemised basket and delivery: order RL-ORDER-44188 delivered 14 April 2025 under DPD consignment 7711224488, and order RL-ORDER-44192 delivered 15 April 2025 under DPD consignment 7711224501. The delivery evidence is merchant-stated on the invoices rather than carrier-issued proof of delivery, but it identifies distinct consignments and distinct dates for each charge.

requirements.title: Timestamps and auth codes
requirements.text: Transaction timestamps and authorisation codes for each charge.
requirements.finding: Each charge carries its own capture timestamp and authorisation code: auth 442189 captured 12 Apr 2025 08:11:33 for order RL-ORDER-44188, and auth 552781 captured 12 Apr 2025 19:42:18 for order RL-ORDER-44192. The disputed transaction txn_5523IJ timestamps to 08:11:33 on 12 April, matching the first capture.

alerts.text: The invoice records the first capture as 08:11:33 BST while transaction metadata records txn_5523IJ as 08:11:33Z (UTC); BST is UTC+1, so the two stamps are nominally an hour apart despite referring to the same capture.

reasons: Every requirement the decision relies on is backed by verified evidence

justification: Both £54.00 charges are documented as distinct orders with different items, order IDs, authorisation codes and separate DPD deliveries, so no duplicate processing occurred.
rationale: The issuer alleges a duplicate £54.00 charge on 12 April 2025. The merchant has evidenced two separate purchases on that date: invoice RL-88291 (order RL-ORDER-44188, coffee beans, £60.00 less a £6.00 loyalty discount) captured at 08:11:33 under auth code 442189 and delivered 14 April 2025 on DPD consignment 7711224488; and invoice RL-88294 (order RL-ORDER-44192, Aeropress Go kit and filter papers) captured at 19:42:18 under auth code 552781 and delivered 15 April 2025 on DPD consignment 7711224501. The matching £54.00 totals are coincidental — different baskets, different order IDs, different authorisation codes, separate deliveries eleven hours and one day apart respectively. The disputed transaction txn_5523IJ (AVS Y, CVV M, 3DS frictionless, billing and shipping both N1 4PD) reconciles to the first capture, and neither charge duplicates the other.
